root.label: Second British Empire
root.gloss: How naval hegemony, Indian de-industrialisation, the 1857 Rebellion, Scramble for Africa, and Drain of Wealth shaped empire.

children.label: Part 1: Maritime & Naval Power
children.gloss: Mercantilist Navigation Acts, Trafalgar, Portsmouth Dockyard mass production, HMS Warrior, and the 1889 Two-Power Standard.

children.label: 1. Naval Power & Portsmouth
children.q2Chain: Mercantilism & 1805 Trafalgar → Portsmouth & 1860 HMS Warrior → 1889 Two-Power Standard
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Mercantilism & 1805 Trafalgar → Portsmouth & 1860 HMS Warrior → 1889 Two-Power Standard.

children.label: Mercantilism & 1805 Trafalgar
children.gloss: Navigation Acts channelled colonial wealth to Britain while Nelson’s 1805 Trafalgar triumph secured a century of sea control.

children.label: Navigation Acts Closed Trade
children.gloss: Barred foreign ships from trade; Funnelled sugar and cotton home.

children.label: 21 Oct 1805 Trafalgar Victory
children.gloss: 27 ships beat 33 Franco-Spanish; Pierced line without losing ship.

children.label: → Secured Century Pax Britannica
children.gloss: Policed global merchant sea lanes; Backed gunboat diplomacy abroad.

children.label: Portsmouth & 1860 HMS Warrior
children.gloss: Portsmouth Dockyard pioneered mass production with Brunel’s block mills before Britain launched ironclad HMS Warrior in 1860.

children.label: 1803 Brunel Steam Block Mills
children.gloss: 10,000 Portsmouth dockyard staff; 130,000 rigging blocks yearly.

children.label: 1860 Ironclad HMS Warrior
children.gloss: 4.5-inch iron over 18-inch teak; Steam screws and rifled guns.

children.label: Made Wooden Battleships Obsolete
children.gloss: Bounced shells in live trials; Kept Britain ahead of France.

children.label: 1889 Two-Power Standard
children.gloss: Challenged by Germany, France, and Russia, Parliament passed the £21.5m Naval Defence Act 1889 to match two rivals combined.

children.label: Rising European Naval Rivals
children.gloss: Germany, France and Russia grew; Threatened imperial sea routes.

children.label: 1889 Naval Defence Act (£21.5m)
children.gloss: Matched next two fleets combined; Built dozens of new battleships.

children.label: Enshrined Deterrence in Statute
children.gloss: Expanded Portsmouth shipyards; Protected global maritime empire.

children.label: Part 2: Company Rule & The Raj
children.gloss: How tariffs and Lancashire mills ruined Indian handlooms, and how Company annexations sparked the 1857 Rebellion and British Raj.

children.label: 2. De-industrialising India
children.q2Chain: Mughal Cloth, Calico Bans & Diwani → Lancashire Mills & 70–80% Tariffs → Dhaka Collapse & Bentinck Note
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Mughal Cloth, Calico Bans & Diwani → Lancashire Mills & 70–80% Tariffs → Dhaka Collapse & Bentinck Note.

children.label: Mughal Cloth, Calico Bans & Diwani
children.gloss: Mughal India made 25% of world cloth until British Calico Acts blocked imports and the 1765 Diwani halted silver inflows.

children.label: Mughal 25% Global Cloth Share
children.gloss: Wove fine muslins and calicoes; Earned European silver bullion.

children.label: 1700 & 1721 Calico Import Bans
children.gloss: Protesting English weavers rioted; Sheltered domestic wool makers.

children.label: → 1765 Diwani Stopped Bullion
children.gloss: Taxed 20 million in Bengal; Bought silk using peasant taxes.

children.label: Lancashire Mills & 70–80% Tariffs
children.gloss: Britain taxed Indian cloth 70–80% while flooding Indian bazaars with 2%-duty Lancashire machine cotton.

children.label: Unequal One-Way Colonial Tariffs
children.gloss: 70–80% tax on Indian imports; 2% duty on Lancashire cotton.

children.label: → Undercut Village Handlooms
children.gloss: Machine yarn flooded bazaars; Priced spinners out of markets.

children.label: Inverted Global Cotton Trade
children.gloss: Turned India into raw supplier; Boosted Manchester mill fortunes.

children.label: Dhaka Collapse & Bentinck Note
children.gloss: Textile hubs like Dhaka emptied into poverty, prompting Bentinck’s 1834 remark on weavers’ bones bleaching Indian plains.

children.label: Dhaka Weaving Centres Deserted
children.gloss: Handloom cloth exports collapsed; Artisans pushed into farm toil.

children.label: 1834 Bentinck Bleaching Plains
children.gloss: Recorded weavers’ mass misery; Confirmed mass textile de-industrialisation.

children.label: → Deepened Anti-Company Anger
children.gloss: Impoverished rural provinces; Fed resentment before 1857.

children.label: 3. 1857 Rebellion & British Raj
children.q2Chain: Doctrine of Lapse & Cartridges → Delhi March & Rani Lakshmibai → 1858 Act & Birth of British Raj
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Doctrine of Lapse & Cartridges → Delhi March & Rani Lakshmibai → 1858 Act & Birth of British Raj.

children.label: Doctrine of Lapse & Cartridges
children.gloss: Dalhousie’s annexations of Jhansi and Awadh combined with cow-and-pig fat rumours on 1857 Enfield cartridges.

children.label: Dalhousie’s Doctrine of Lapse
children.gloss: Annexed Satara, Jhansi and Awadh; Disinherited adopted Hindu heirs.

children.label: 1857 Greased Enfield Cartridges
children.gloss: Bitten tubes rumoured animal fat; Offended Hindu and Muslim faiths.

children.label: → Sparked 10 May Meerut Mutiny
children.gloss: 85 jailed sepoys freed at Meerut; Marched overnight to take Delhi.

children.label: Delhi March & Rani Lakshmibai
children.gloss: Rebels rallied around Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar in Delhi while Rani Lakshmibai led fierce resistance from Jhansi to Gwalior.

children.label: Bahadur Shah II Named Sovereign
children.gloss: United Hindu and Muslim rebels; Spread war across north plains.

children.label: Rani Lakshmibai Fought to 1858
children.gloss: Escaped Jhansi walls with child; Killed fighting at Gwalior.

children.label: Shattered Company Legitimacy
children.gloss: Nearly toppled British control; Became anti-colonial hero.

children.label: 1858 Act & Birth of British Raj
children.gloss: Parliament abolished the East India Company in August 1858, placing India under direct Crown and Viceroy rule.

children.label: 1858 Act Dissolved the Company
children.gloss: Transferred rule to Queen Victoria; Ruled through royal Viceroy.

children.label: → Victoria Promised Toleration
children.gloss: Halted princely state seizures; Pledged non-interference in faith.

children.label: Entrenched Segregated Raj Rule
children.gloss: Deepened strict racial hierarchy; Backed by British garrison force.

children.label: Part 3: Africa & Empire Verdict
children.gloss: The 1884 Berlin Conference, Maxim guns, Congo rubber terror, Dadabhai Naoroji’s Drain of Wealth, and modern Empire debates.

children.label: 4. Scramble for Africa
children.q2Chain: 1884 Berlin & Occupation Rule → Maxim Gun, Quinine & Kipling → Rubber Quotas & Congo Terror
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1884 Berlin & Occupation Rule → Maxim Gun, Quinine & Kipling → Rubber Quotas & Congo Terror.

children.label: 1884 Berlin & Occupation Rule
children.gloss: Fourteen Western powers met in Berlin with zero Africans invited, mandating inland Effective Occupation to claim territory.

children.label: 1884 Berlin 14-Nation Partition
children.gloss: Hosted by Otto von Bismarck; Zero African leaders invited.

children.label: Effective Occupation Requirement
children.gloss: Demanded inland forts and flags; Ended coast-only treaty claims.

children.label: → Armed Race into Interior
children.gloss: Drew straight map border lines; Split African kingdoms apart.

children.label: Maxim Gun, Quinine & Kipling
children.gloss: Quinine and 600-rpm Maxim guns crushed African armies at Omdurman while Kipling’s 1899 poem preached racial duty.

children.label: Quinine & 600-RPM Maxim Gun
children.gloss: Cinchona bark stopped malaria; 10,000 killed at 1898 Omdurman.

children.label: 1899 White Man’s Burden Poem
children.gloss: Kipling claimed civilising duty; Used half-devil racial slur.

children.label: Masked Conquest as Moral Duty
children.gloss: Paired machine guns and racism; Alibied imperial land seizures.

children.label: Rubber Quotas & Congo Terror
children.gloss: Colonial regimes looted rubber, ivory, and diamonds through forced labour, killing up to ten million in Leopold II’s Congo.

children.label: Looted Rubber, Palm Oil & Ivory
children.gloss: Used forced labour and taxes; Enriched European tycoons.

children.label: Leopold II’s Congo Free State
children.gloss: Hostages and severed hands terror; Estimated ten million perished.

children.label: → Exposed Civilising Hypocrisy
children.gloss: Campaigned against by E.D. Morel; Revealed violent extraction truth.

children.label: 5. The Imperial Verdict
children.q2Chain: 1851 Exhibition & Rail Network → 1876 Famines & Naoroji’s Drain → Ferguson vs Tharoor Verdict
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1851 Exhibition & Rail Network → 1876 Famines & Naoroji’s Drain → Ferguson vs Tharoor Verdict.

children.label: 1851 Exhibition & Rail Network
children.gloss: The 1851 Crystal Palace celebrated Britain’s Workshop of the World while engineers built 25,000 miles of Indian railways.

children.label: 1851 Crystal Palace Exhibition
children.gloss: 6 million visited Hyde Park; Displayed looted Koh-i-Noor gem.

children.label: 25,000 Miles of Indian Railways
children.gloss: Added canals and telegraphs; Linked inland farms to ports.

children.label: Development vs Military Control
children.gloss: Integrated distant Indian markets; Moved troops and export crops.

children.label: 1876 Famines & Naoroji’s Drain
children.gloss: Ten million starved under Lytton’s free-market famine policy while MP Dadabhai Naoroji proved Britain’s Drain of Wealth.

children.label: 1876–78 Famines & Grain Exports
children.gloss: Viceroy Lytton kept free trade; 10m died while wheat exported.

children.label: Naoroji’s Drain of Wealth Proof
children.gloss: First Indian MP in 1892; Tax money funded London wars.

children.label: → Galvanized Self-Rule Critique
children.gloss: Demolished benevolent-rule myth; Demanded Indian political rights.

children.label: Ferguson vs Tharoor Verdict
children.gloss: Niall Ferguson highlights common law and railways, whereas Shashi Tharoor condemns de-industrialisation, tax drain, and famine.

children.label: Optimist Case (Niall Ferguson)
children.gloss: Spread common law and trade; Built railways and telegraphs.

children.label: Pessimist Case (Shashi Tharoor)
children.gloss: Crushed weavers; drained taxes; Caused preventable mass famines.

children.label: Weighing Modernisation vs Cost
children.gloss: Contrasts rail lines with famine; Drives ongoing empire debate.
